definition: XCES is an XML based standard to encode text corpora, which are used by linguists and natural language researchers.
details: XCES is highly based on the previous EAGLES Corpus Encoding Standard (CES) but uses XML as the markup language. It supports simple corpora as well as annotated corpora, parallel corpora and other.

explainer.lead: XCES is an XML-based standard for encoding text corpora used by linguists and natural language researchers. It matters because it gives annotated and parallel text collections a common, machine-readable format.

tiers.eli5: It is a shared filing system for collections of text, so different research teams can read each other's documents without retyping them.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers use it to store corpora, including annotated and parallel versions, in XML for reuse across tools. The pitfall is that XML markup is verbose, so large corpora become bulky.
tiers.paperLevel: A corpus encoding standard built on XML, derived from the earlier EAGLES Corpus Encoding Standard (CES). It covers simple corpora, annotated corpora and parallel corpora, but is not a model or algorithm.

explainer.example: A parallel corpus of aligned sentences in two languages is stored in XCES XML so each sentence pair can be matched by tools.
